name: Albany International Airport
notes: Official page https://www.albanyairport.com/airport-amenities/interfaith-prayer-room read 18 Oct 2026. Quote: "The Interfaith Prayer Room is now located on the first floor of Concourse A, offering travelers a more comfortable and accessible space for prayer, meditation, and reflection." It says visitors "may find prayer rugs, talitot, kipot, rosary beads and other items" and that books including "the Koran" are available, and that "The Interfaith Prayer Room is open daily." The page does not say whether the room is before or after security, and wudu facilities, a women's area and qibla marking are not described. The main Airport Guide page (https://www.albanyairport.com/airport-guide) does not list the room; it is linked from the amenities sub-pages. A separate Sensory Room is also listed (not a prayer space). Contact link on the site points to the About ALB page; phone (518) 242-2222, info@albanyairport.com.

name: Birmingham-Shuttlesworth International Airport

spaces.name: Meditation Room
spaces.location: unknown (the official page does not give a location)

notes: Official Amenities page https://flybirmingham.com/amenities read 18 Oct 2026. Quote: "When you need to get away from the hustle and bustle of airport travel, we have a dedicated meditation room, designed to offer passengers a quiet escape." That one sentence is the only mention; I also searched the site's whole public content store (the Sanity CMS behind flybirmingham.com) and the terminal-maps and accessibility pages, and none gives the room's location, hours or security side. The same page lists nursing rooms (Concourse B near the Food Court and Concourse C near Gate C1) and a sensory room for travelers with autism and special needs (not a prayer space). Ask at the information desk for the location.

name: Boise Airport

name: Gerald R. Ford International Airport

spaces.name: Sensory Room
spaces.location: Beginning of Concourse A; entry by a call button next to the door
spaces.type: quiet seating (sensory room for travelers with sensory sensitivities; not described for prayer)

notes: Official Amenities page https://www.grr.org/amenities and FAQ https://www.grr.org/faq read 18 Oct 2026. No chapel, prayer, meditation or reflection room is listed. The only quiet space is the Sensory Room: "located at the beginning of Concourse A. This new area is designed to offer support to travelers with sensory sensitivities"; "The Sensory Room is open to travelers and can be accessed through a call button next to the entrance door." It is built for travelers with cognitive or developmental disabilities, with four zones, so it is listed as quiet seating only. Nursing rooms are pre-security near GRR Life Market & Cafe and post-security across from Starbucks in the Marketplace. The site search (HubSpot) works ("nursing" returns Amenities) and returned nothing for chapel, meditation or interfaith; "prayer" returned only a sculpture news story.
